name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,360

clue.text: Some beer not originally for bird

indicators.note: what comes originally comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: bitter is a type of British ale, so some beer
the first letter of not

explanation.surface: Someone is offering a drop of ale that was not first meant for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is the hoppy draught ale of British pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading heron-family species known for its booming call in reedbeds.

clue.text: Growth of deficit in endless pots of money

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped
in places the first word inside the trimmed second

blocks.note: a deficit is a loss
a bomb is British slang for a large sum, as in cost a bomb

explanation.surface: A financial report on how a shortfall grew inside a seemingly bottomless fund.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, something that costs a bomb is very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossom is the flowering of a plant, a kind of growth, and as a verb also means to develop.

clue.text: Set fair?

blocks.note: surface reading: a weather forecast promising settled sunshine
setter's reading: looking good on the television set

explanation.walkthrough: Set fair is a barometer phrase for steady fine weather; here set is a TV set and fair means good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone telegenic has a look and manner that comes across attractively on television screens.

clue.text: End of unlimited messages associated with army engineers

indicators.note: with no limits means both boundary letters are removed

blocks.note: texts are phone messages
the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: An end to the endless texts from soldiers in the engineering corps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' looks like a letter-picking instruction; End is in fact the definition. REME, not the usual RE, supplies the army engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: The extreme of something is its furthest point or limit, its very end.

clue.text: Catches North American deceptive humbug over the pond

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for North American
BS is American slang for nonsense; over the pond means across the Atlantic

explanation.surface: An American catches out a fraudulent piece of hypocrisy.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab someone is to seize or arrest them, so the verb means catches.

clue.text: Trace deep source of pain

blocks.note: a whit is the tiniest amount, a trace
a deep voice or note is low

explanation.surface: A doctor follows a faint sign of a deep-seated ache to its origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitlow is an infected, throbbing swelling beside a fingernail, so it is a painful sore.

clue.text: Wished to go mad with domestic appliances?

indicators.note: going mad means losing order, so the letters come out scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was so fed up with their kitchen machines they longed to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: White goods is the trade term for large household machines such as fridges, washers and cookers.

clue.text: Admit to where wires may go?

blocks.note: first meaning: formally bring someone into an office or society
second meaning, split as two words: inside a channel for cables

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer as IN DUCT; electrical wiring is run through ducts, and the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: To induct someone is to install or formally receive them into a post or organisation.

clue.text: Permission to abandon farewell holiday

blocks.note: first meaning: consent
second meaning: time off

explanation.walkthrough: Every word in the clue is a sense of the answer: to abandon (to go away from) and farewell (to take one's leave) are further meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave means both consent to do something and an authorised period of absence from work.

clue.text: Flier with report of what to do with vacant property?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are taken by their spoken sound

blocks.clueFragment: what to do with vacant property
blocks.note: an empty house should be let to tenants

explanation.surface: A landlord gets advice on what to do with an empty house.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole bird name is said like the advice to let a property out.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrentit is a small long-tailed songbird of the American west coast, so a flying creature.

clue.text: Anything about the Italian winger?

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything
le is an Italian plural form of the, as in le donne

explanation.surface: A question about anything concerning an Italian footballer playing out wide.
explanation.walkthrough: Owt (anything) and nowt (nothing) are Yorkshire dialect words loved by setters.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is a winged creature, and setters often call any bird a winger or flier.

clue.text: TV programme could get cavorting lad in debt

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about wildly, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young man fooling around on television might end up owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: Blind Date was a long-running British Saturday-night dating show hosted by Cilla Black.
explanation.definitionFit: The show is a named television series in which contestants picked partners they could not see.

clue.text: Proceeds without a pause to accommodate house guests - on the contrary

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house within, so the letters sit inside the neighbouring words
this flips the apparent direction: the clue words do the housing, not the answer

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Someone moves straight on to finding room for visitors, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read naively, the answer would house the guests; the contrary is that the phrase house guests holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To segue is to move smoothly from one thing to the next without stopping, as a DJ does between tracks.

clue.text: Teaches about property reverting to the Crown

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A law lecturer gives classes on land that returns to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Escheat is the legal term for an estate passing to the state or lord when there is no heir.

clue.text: Saint bears tipsy Rechabites ...

indicators.note: someone tipsy staggers about, so the letters reel out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A holy man puts up with members of a temperance sect who are drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rechabites were a biblical clan who drank no wine, and the name was taken by a temperance society.
explanation.definitionFit: Rechabites renounce alcohol entirely, so they are teetotallers who refuse all drink.

clue.text: African leader abridged books about British mathematician

indicators.note: an abridged text is cut short, so the name loses its final letter

blocks.note: Nelson Mandela, South Africa's first black president
standard abbreviation for British
the Old Testament books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A shortened biography of an African statesman is reviewed alongside one on a British scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British mathematician' reads as one phrase, but British is wordplay; about here just means next to, so the books sit beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Benoit Mandelbrot was the Polish-born French-American who developed fractal geometry, giving the Mandelbrot set.

clue.text: Hit heartless drip

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word is taken out

blocks.note: to sweat is to drip with perspiration

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a feeble, wet person without any compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: A drip is also a feeble person, which sets up the cruel picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To swat is to strike sharply, as with a flat object against a fly.

clue.text: ... drunk as they might be after much practice

definitions.text: as they might be after much practice

blocks.note: first meaning: thoroughly intoxicated

blocks.clueFragment: as they might be after much practice
blocks.note: second meaning: running smoothly, like a well-rehearsed machine

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the teetotallers, so the abstainers are pictured drunk; a team after long rehearsal runs like a smooth machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for intoxicated and also describes something that operates smoothly through experience.

clue.text: Commune excluded from brief treaty

indicators.note: something excluded from a word is taken out of it, leaving the rest

blocks.note: com. is an abbreviation for commune
compact means concise, brief

explanation.surface: A French commune is left out of a short international agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement between parties, the same thing as a treaty.

clue.text: Plymouth Brethren consuming different plant

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so the abbreviation swallows the other word

blocks.note: PB is the abbreviation for the Plymouth Brethren sect
other means different

explanation.surface: Members of a strict Christian sect eat an unfamiliar plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot herb is a leafy plant grown for cooking, such as a herb or green vegetable.

clue.text: Stupidly fail to dust apartment

indicators.note: doing something stupidly makes a mess of it, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lazy tenant foolishly neglects the cleaning in their home.
explanation.walkthrough: A studio flat is the British term for a one-room apartment with a kitchen area.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a small self-contained dwelling, the British equivalent of a studio apartment.

clue.text: Old greenery rector removed behind schedule

indicators.note: something removed is taken away, so its letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for old
verdure is lush green vegetation
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: The vicarage's old shrubbery has been cleared away much later than planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has not arrived or been done by the expected time, so it is late.

clue.text: Potentially make it a target

indicators.note: potentially means what could be, so the letters may become something else

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has a goal in mind that they could choose to pursue.
explanation.walkthrough: Target is a verb here, not the noun it seems to be.
explanation.definitionFit: To take aim is to point a weapon at something, which is what targeting it means.

clue.text: Spot bulletin

blocks.note: first meaning: catch sight of, observe
second meaning: a posted announcement

explanation.walkthrough: Spot reads as a noun beside bulletin, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for observing something and a noun for a written public announcement.

clue.text: After end of Act 1, playwright enters with ice cream

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
something that enters goes inside, so the name sits between the other letters

blocks.note: the final letter of Act
Joe Orton, English writer of Loot and Entertaining Mr Sloane
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: After the first act finishes, the dramatist arrives with an interval ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act 1' looks like one theatrical phrase, but the end of Act and the 1 are separate pieces that the playwright goes between.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortoni is an Italian frozen dessert of cream and macaroons, a type of ice cream.

clue.text: Bake rhubarb containing a dash of sugar

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the nonsense word wraps the other letters
a dash is a tiny splash, so just the opening letter is used

blocks.note: rhubarb is British slang for nonsense, as is rot
taken as written
the first letter of sugar

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to cook rhubarb with a sprinkle of sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhubarb looks like the fruit to be baked; in Britain it also means nonsense, like rot.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook in an oven with dry heat, much as baking does.

clue.text: Change divinity lesson?

blocks.note: RE is religious education, the school subject once called divinity
lessons are schoolwork

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a religious studies class has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: RE work is what a pupil does in a divinity lesson; the question mark flags that cryptic reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To rework something is to revise or alter it, so it means to change.

clue.text: Italy has to replace the French in union? Really!

indicators.note: to replace means one thing is swapped in where another stood

blocks.note: ASLEF is the British train drivers' trade union
le is French for the
I is the international car code for Italy

explanation.surface: An incredulous question about Italy displacing France within the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The EU springs to mind for union, but it is ASLEF, the British rail drivers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'as if!' expresses scornful disbelief, like a sarcastic 'really!'.

clue.text: Analysts finding measure of radiation in old chemicals

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the unit sits within the chemicals

blocks.note: ex means former, old
amines are organic compounds derived from ammonia
R is the symbol for the roentgen, a unit of radiation exposure

explanation.surface: Scientists find radiation readings in some outdated chemical samples.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners scrutinise and assess things in detail, just as analysts study data.

clue.text: Cook's haircut interrupted by old priest

indicators.note: when one thing is interrupted by another, the second breaks into its middle

blocks.note: a DA, or duck's arse, is a 1950s greased-back hairstyle
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A chef's trim at the barber's is cut short by an elderly clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is Britain's best-known television cookery writer, so Cook's reads as Cook is.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia Smith is a famous British cookery author, so the name stands for a cook by example.

clue.text: Former Conservative minister's servants

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to Rab Butler, the post-war Tory Chancellor and Home Secretary
second meaning: chief manservants of a household

explanation.surface: A retired Tory politician's household staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab Butler was a leading British Conservative minister of the 1950s and 60s; the possessive gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The head manservants in grand households are called by this title, and the surname of the Tory statesman matches it.

clue.text: Regularly force feed tommy with permission

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Someone routinely force-feeds a British soldier once they have been allowed to.
explanation.walkthrough: A tommy is a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom to do something is licence or leave to do it, so the word can mean permission.
